# pipensx 1.7.1

Changes since the last published GitLab release, 1.6.6.

## Catalog and game details

- Search ranks close title matches and compares related releases.
- Catalog cards show cached peer counts, collections, and attributed Metacritic
  scores. Multi-title releases retain their individual title IDs and versions.
- Catalog downloads can fall back to the GitHub contents API and the GitLab
  mirror. Cached snapshots and diffs are checked for provenance and age.
- Game details distinguish download size from the space required by selected
  packages, show title revisions, and link to the source topic through a QR code.
- File selection uses the available screen height, groups nested files, and
  warns about overlapping update selections before installation.

## Downloads and appearance

- Download cards show live peer statistics and retain network information while
  seeding. Secondary details can be expanded when needed.
- Verified pieces can be shared from RAM and SD storage. Peer discovery and
  incoming connections have received fixes.
- Uncached debrid torrents can remain in the provider queue.
- 7z archive header reads and writes no longer rely on unaligned integer
  pointer accesses.
- Added appearance themes and configurable accent colors. Theme changes apply
  after restarting pipensx.
- Added screen blanking during transfers and optional sleep after the queue
  finishes.

## Web Companion

- Manage downloads, browse the catalog and installed library, select files,
  change console settings, inspect logs, and run maintenance from a browser.
- Download a catalog through the phone or computer connection and upload it to
  the Switch. Local catalog JSON files are also supported, up to 48 MiB.
- Download the latest pipensx NRO and its checksum through the browser. The
  console verifies SHA-256 before staging the replacement.
- Upload a local NRO, then replace and restart through the existing updater.
  After the helper returns to HOME, launch pipensx again on the Switch.
- The update helper exits the application process, preventing forwarders from
  relaunching pipensx in the same loader session and crashing after replacement.
- Idle HTTP connections yield their slots to new requests, avoiding unnecessary
  busy responses while preserving active uploads and event streams.

Browser downloads use that device's connection, including its VPN. The VPN must
allow access to the Switch on the local network. If a source blocks browser
downloads through CORS, download the file separately and use the file picker.

## Installation

Copy `switch/pipensx/pipensx.nro` from `SDOut.zip` to the SD card, or replace the
existing NRO with the standalone `pipensx.nro`. Keep the existing pipensx data
directory to preserve settings, cached artwork, and download state. The public
build fetches its catalog on first use and does not bundle games or firmware.

Upgrading the published 1.6.6 build to 1.7.1 through Web Companion's NRO upload
and apply actions was tested on a physical Switch. The installed NRO checksum,
settings, and all six existing tasks were verified after the upgrade.

An older development build's helper did crash after replacement during a
separate test. If this happens, dismiss the error and launch pipensx again
from HOME; the file-copy method above is also available. Version 1.7.1 supplies
the corrected helper for subsequent updates.

# pipensx [![CI](https://github.com/i3sey/pipensx/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/i3sey/pipensx/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: GPL-3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPL--3.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/i3sey/pipensx)](https://github.com/i3sey/pipensx/releases/latest) Native BitTorrent download manager and streaming package installer for Nintendo Switch homebrew. DOWNLOAD LATEST - [pipensx.nro](https://github.com/i3sey/pipensx/releases/latest/download/pipensx.nro)

> [!IMPORTANT] > pipensx does not include Nintendo keys, firmware, games, or a torrent catalog. > Use it only with content you are legally allowed to download and install. The > project is not affiliated with Nintendo, RuTracker, or the catalog provider. > [!NOTE] > This project was developed with substantial assistance from AI tools for code > generation, refactoring, testing, review, and documentation. Changes are > still built and validated before they are merged. ## Features - native Borealis interface with controller, touch, light/dark, handheld, and docked support - persistent FIFO queue with pause, resume, retry, recheck, and safe shutdown - redesigned Downloads workspace with live category filters (All, Active, Queued, Finished, Errors) - refined Installed Games view with direct actions (Open in catalog, Update, Ignore, Uninstall) and facts table - restart-safe piece verification and download recovery - tracker, DHT, and PEX peer discovery - live, cached catalog loaded from the trusted Langegen catalog with cover URLs - offline magnet resolution when the catalog provides a verified info dictionary - download-only mode and sequential NSP/NSZ installation while pieces arrive - unified homebrew-port installs: NRO application folders and ZIP/7z payloads are deployed safely to `SD:/switch/` before local NSP/NSZ forwarders install - Application, Patch, and AddOnContent packages with installed-version checks - optional debrid fetch via TorBox, Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, or a self-hosted TorrServer - optional HTTPS/SOCKS proxy for catalog, artwork, and debrid HTTPS traffic - download diagnostics, speed history, peer state, and extended telemetry The public build intentionally starts without a bundled catalog. On first use, the Catalog view refreshes from the trusted Langegen source and then uses its on-SD cache. Open **Settings → Catalog → Catalog source** to choose GitHub (global), GitLab (global), or GitVerse (Russia, marked with the Russian flag). Built-in mirrors follow the catalog language. If the selected mirror fails or returns invalid JSON, the app tries the other mirrors and retains the cached catalog if all fail. The selected preference stays unchanged. **Custom URL** accepts an HTTPS JSON URL and uses only that source. Updating the catalog includes its cover URLs without a separate artwork update. The **Homebrew** tab has a separate app catalog with search, descriptions and direct NRO/ZIP installation. Downloads are checked against their SHA-256 before files are written to the SD card. See [Homebrew catalog](docs/HOMEBREW.md) for file replacement rules and system-module handling. ## Quick start [GitHub](https://github.com/i3sey/pipensx) is the primary repository hosting development, CI, issues, pull requests, and releases. [GitLab](https://gitlab.com/pipensx-group/pipensx) and local Gitea (`git@192.168.1.146:i3sey/pipensx.git`) are maintained as backup mirrors. See [BUILD.md](BUILD.md#development-remotes) for remote setup. Clone the pinned submodules: ```bash git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/i3sey/pipensx.git cd pipensx ``` Run the portable PC test suite: ```bash make test ``` Build the Nintendo Switch application after installing devkitPro dependencies: ```bash export DEVKITPRO=/opt/devkitpro make switch ``` The resulting application is `build-switch/pipensx.nro`. See [BUILD.md](BUILD.md) for dependency installation, optional metadata input, and deployment helpers. ## Install on Nintendo Switch Download the latest [pipensx.nro](https://github.com/i3sey/pipensx/releases/latest/download/pipensx.nro) and copy it to: ```text SD:/switch/pipensx/pipensx.nro ``` Launch it through hbmenu in **application mode** by holding `R` while opening a game. Album applet mode is rejected because it does not provide enough memory and network resources for the application. Runtime data is stored below `SD:/switch/pipensx/`, including: ```text queue.bencode torrents/ downloads/ task-files/ deployments/ dht_nodes.bin catalog/catalog.json catalog/metadata/ catalog/images/ pipensx.log ``` The interface displays contextual controller hints. The main actions cover adding torrents, opening details, pausing/resuming, retrying/rechecking, and safely stopping the active task before exit. ## Ports, mods, and translations Installing a homebrew port offers **Try automatic install** or **Download only**. Automatic installation downloads the selected payload, copies or extracts it to the SD card, and then installs bundled NSP/NSZ forwarders without another confirmation. Download only leaves the files in the downloads folder. **Select files** lets you choose **Install**, **Download**, or **Skip** for each file. Install is available for NSP/NSZ, recognized NRO application files, ZIP/7z payloads, and supported LayeredFS mods and translations. Installing an NRO also selects its companion application files; individual choices can then be adjusted. Applying Install to a folder installs supported files and downloads the rest. Selected installation actions run automatically after downloading. When a regular game release includes installable extras, Install offers the normal recommended game packages without extras, or the manual file selector. Executable patches remain an explicit choice in the selector. If automatic deployment fails, the application reports the reason and retains downloaded files. The web panel remains available for custom destination folders. ## Catalog and network behavior The [web companion](docs/REMOTE_LIBRARY.md) provides queue controls, file selection, catalog favorites and batch adding, installed-title management, console settings, storage cleanup, and diagnostics from a phone or computer on the same network. Maintenance can replace the running NRO with a local file, including an older or identical version. After applying it, reopen pipensx on the Switch; the browser reconnects when the application returns. AutoRun is hidden in the web UI. The application fetches a language-specific catalog over HTTPS from Langegen by default. It tries GitHub Raw, then the GitHub API, then a stored GitLab mirror snapshot with size and SHA-256 verification. See [Catalog mirror](docs/CATALOG_MIRROR.md) for publication and refresh behavior. The deprecated pipensx-catalog release channel checks a manifest first and downloads its catalog only when the SHA-256 changes. Settings let you point at any other HTTPS URL that serves the same JSON shape. Redirects are limited to the source file's directory, except the exact fallback resources of Langegen and the release-asset hosts of the built-in release channel; look-alike hosts are rejected before catalog bytes are parsed. A failed refresh leaves the last valid SD-card cache active. Catalog magnets are resolved from a pre-verified info dictionary when one is available, otherwise through BitTorrent extension-protocol peers. Received metadata is checked against the magnet info hash before entering the normal torrent preview and queue flow. One to four downloads may run concurrently, while stream installation remains serialized. Existing files are verified before a task starts or resumes. Interrupted package streams resume from their last persisted safe point; packages committed before the interruption remain installed and are skipped. On **Downloads**, **Blank screen** controls the display only while downloads or installation are active. Both modes prevent automatic sleep during that work. When enabled, the screen turns off three seconds after the button is pressed. Touch, a controller button, or a stick wakes it; the wake input is absorbed until release, followed by a 300 ms guard. The screen turns off again after seven seconds of inactivity. The selection survives restarts and leaves normal idle settings in control when no download or installation is active. **Settings → Downloads → Sleep after downloads finish** is off by default, so completed torrents can keep seeding. Enable it to request system sleep after the whole queue, including installation, finishes successfully. Paused, failed, or deleted tasks do not trigger sleep. Application mode requires firmware 10.0.0 or later; applet mode requires 15.0.0 or later. If sleep is unavailable or the request fails, pipensx reports the failure and keeps running. In **Settings → Source**, enable **Keep uncached torrents in debrid** to retain unfinished transfers in your provider account when metadata resolution times out or you cancel or exit preparation. Pending entries reuse the saved transfer ID or match an existing TorBox transfer by info-hash on return, prune automatically after 7 days, and can be inspected or removed from **Settings → Source → Pending cloud caches**. Cloud caching and any required file selection follow the provider's rules; the option is off by default. Runtime behavior such as sleep/wake, long installs, and `/switch` file copying must ultimately be validated on physical Switch hardware. ## Contributing and security Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before sending a change. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md); do not place secrets or copyrighted datasets in issues or fixtures. Historical implementation notes are archived under [`docs/plans/`](docs/plans/README.md). They are not the current roadmap. ## License pipensx is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party components retain their original licenses as listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
